events.headline: Chip stocks fall again as Micron drops on Chinese DRAM competition fears (ChangXin Memory progress), dragging SK Hynix, Intel, AMD, Marvell
Big bank earnings mixed: JPMorgan misses EPS but rallies on raised NII guidance; Goldman Sachs beats on profit, as Q3 earnings season opens
10-year Treasury yield climbs to ~5.24% as NY Fed's John Williams says one more rate hike is still appropriate this year, pressuring growth/tech stocks
Johnson & Johnson shares drop roughly 6% after its MedTech division missed sales estimates
Oil stays elevated on persistent Mideast tension (Iran-Israel linked tanker attacks, fading US-Iran peace-deal hopes); Brent topped $105 earlier this week
China's pause on expanded rare-earth/battery-material export controls holds for now but is set to expire Nov 7-10, 2026, keeping supply-chain risk elevated for non-Chinese materials producers
